preamble: In Maltese, the voiced pharyngeal /ʕ/ inherited from Arabic (spelled għ) was lost as a consonant, but before an original *i it left a lengthened open-mid front vowel [ɛː], so that Arabic ʕinab 'grapes' corresponds to Maltese għeneb /ˈɛːnɛp/. Strictly the process is ʕ > ∅ with lowering and compensatory lengthening of the neighbouring vowel; older Maltese still had a pharyngealized [ɛˤː]. It is filed here following the atlas convention for guttural reflexes (compare ain_to_e for the Akkadian e-coloring and ain_to_a).
phoneticEffects: Guttural Loss, Vowel Lowering, Compensatory Lengthening
